answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because wharf only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, trellis is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any nectar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
